clue.text: See 5
European working under North American general

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece placed under another follows it in the answer

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A continental employee takes orders from an American general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places POLE and ON beneath NA in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the famous French military commander.

clue.text: They conceal privates and fighters

definitions.meaning: boxer shorts are underpants covering the private parts
pugilists who fight in a ring

explanation.surface: Something that hides soldiers of low rank and combatants.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are underwear hiding one's private parts, and boxers are prizefighters.

clue.text: Understood 1d?

definitions.meaning: grasped or worked out in one's head
read not as a cross-reference but literally: the numeral 1 is a figure, followed by the letter d

explanation.surface: Asks whether the actress at 1 down was grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: '1d' looks like a pointer to another clue, but read literally it is a figure followed by D.
explanation.definitionFit: To have figured something out is to have worked it out and grasped it.

clue.text: Was she busy modelling Sue in Are You Being Served?

definitions.text: Was she busy modelling Sue in Are You Being Served?

indicators.note: busy letters are bustling about, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a sitcom actress was kept occupied posing as a character named Sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges MODELLING SUE; the whole clue then points to the actress in the sitcom, a 1970s BBC comedy set in a London department store.
explanation.definitionFit: Mollie Sugden played Mrs Slocombe in the BBC department-store sitcom Are You Being Served?

clue.text: Local resident in antique country

indicators.note: something resident in another lives inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: an antique is an old relic
a local is a British name for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: A villager living in an old-fashioned rural area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective but is the British word for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation without a monarch.

clue.text: Very small vehicle reversing by a cat, I see

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a tom is a male cat
the letter C sounds like the word see

explanation.surface: A driver notices a tiny car backing into a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Subatomic particles are smaller than atoms, so extremely tiny.

clue.text: One getting some orders around the summit of Sinai?

definitions.text: One getting some orders around the summit of Sinai?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the other piece
to order is to arrange, so the word some is rearranged
the summit is the top, so the first letter of Sinai is taken

explanation.surface: Someone receiving commandments up on the mountaintop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' rearranges SOME into MOES, and 'around' wraps it round S, the top of Sinai; the clue as a whole describes the receiving of the Ten Commandments.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the prophet received the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai.

clue.text: They don't fit plywood, done outside or inside

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words plywood, done outside

explanation.surface: Some timber panels will not slot in, whether placed outdoors or in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like part of the outdoor-or-indoor choice but signals the run of letters within the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the odd one out differs from the rest of its group and fails to fit.

clue.text: Show contempt for loud hooligan

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
a lout is a rough, boorish hooligan

explanation.surface: Despising a noisy yob.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule is to disregard it openly, showing scorn for it.

clue.text: Building weapon unleashes anger

indicators.note: to unleash anger is to let it out, so ire leaves the weapon

parts.note: a firearm is a gun, a weapon
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone constructing a weapon lets their rage loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm is a rural holding, and the word also names its house and buildings, as in a farmhouse.

clue.text: England's in trouble, wanting Norway and Germany as financial backers

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so some letters are removed from the jumble

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: England's team struggles, needing two other European nations to bankroll it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges ENGLANDS, and 'wanting' takes out N and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels are private investors who fund theatre shows or new businesses.

clue.text: Close to dive 50, T Daley dances with joy

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of dive is taken

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so T Daley is rearranged

explanation.surface: British diver Tom Daley celebrates after nearly nailing a dive scoring fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges T DALEY into ATEDLY. Tom Daley is a British Olympic diver.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something elatedly means in high spirits, happily.

clue.text: Might this show you're married to Chuck?

definitions.meaning: a wedding band worn on the finger signals marriage
to chuck is to throw away or give up

explanation.surface: Whether a sign shows you are wed to someone named Chuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a husband's name but is the verb meaning discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to desert or discard it, as one chucks it.

clue.text: Mountain in Germany, yes? I'm climbing with new boy

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
ja is German for yes

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upwards, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A German mountaineer agrees he is going up with a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin is a boy's given name, and the youngest son of Jacob.

clue.text: Could be expensive round — drink up …

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Buying a round of drinks could cost a lot, so drink up.
explanation.definitionFit: This gemstone is an example of something that may be costly, as precious stones often are.

clue.text: Incriminate every individual backing Independence politician

indicators.note: a piece backing another goes behind it

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independence or independent
an MP is a Member of Parliament
each means every individual one

explanation.surface: Accusing all those who support an independence-minded politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach an official is to formally charge them with wrongdoing.

clue.text: … only ten pound, I count

indicators.note: to pound is to beat, so the letters of ten are battered into a new order

parts.note: to count on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Continuing the drinking: just ten pounds, I reckon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like the currency but rearranges TEN into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly or solely, as in a decision resting only on you.

clue.text: Wild plants caught by Romeo and Juliet?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Shakespeare's pair are the most famous young lovers

explanation.surface: Wildflowers scooped up by the star-crossed couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a meadow plant of the trefoil family that grows freely in grassland.

clue.text: Drink with little chance of being found in Hell?

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade

definitions.text: little chance of being found in Hell?
definitions.meaning: from the idiom a ... chance in hell, meaning no chance at all

explanation.surface: A beverage that is unlikely to exist in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a Christmas cocktail and the icy ball that would melt in an inferno.

clue.text: Doctor works and cries at mistake

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC time-travelling hero
ops, short for opuses, are works

explanation.surface: A physician operates and wails at an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' gives WHO from the TV series Doctor Who, a long-running BBC science-fiction show.
explanation.definitionFit: These are exclamations people utter on blundering or dropping something.

clue.text: Common umlaut design

indicators.note: to design is to arrange, so the letters of umlaut are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A typographer remarks on a frequent accent mark pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual means shared, as in common interests or a common friend.

clue.text: Spoon bender hugged by little girl, then another

indicators.note: being hugged means held inside, so one name sits within the other

parts.note: Mel is a short form of the girl's name Melanie
Uri Geller is famous for bending spoons

explanation.surface: A celebrity spoon bender gets cuddles from one young girl after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' refers back to the little girl: the answer is another girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel is a female first name, so one more girl in addition to Mel.

clue.text: A game, a lake, a creature

parts.note: nim is a game of taking objects from heaps
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A list of things: a pastime, a body of water, a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a living creature such as a beast.

clue.text: A great prime minister?

definitions.meaning: John ... was UK prime minister from 1990 to 1997

explanation.surface: Asks whether a premier was outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means large or important, and John Major led the British government in the 1990s.

clue.text: Exercise too much? It's evident — need shower

parts.note: overt means open and evident
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: After working out too hard it's clear you need a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' suggests a wash after the gym but means a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to work out to excess, beyond what the body can recover from.

clue.text: Lover of the '60s, Carpenter gives up crown

indicators.note: the crown is the top, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: chippy is British slang for a carpenter

explanation.surface: A woodworker who loves the 1960s abdicates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpenter' looks like a name (the Carpenters) but is CHIPPY, British slang for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippies were the 1960s flower-power counterculture devoted to peace and love.

clue.text: Gold — good and fashionable when worn by adult, 1984-style

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
well means good, in good health

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone surrounds them, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: in means fashionable
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Gold, fine and trendy when sported by a grown-up, in the manner of a famous novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwellian describes the totalitarian surveillance pictured in George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.
